To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of session types in a language for object-oriented distributed computing is a promising direction to explore, and that the use of sessions in an object-oriented language can be used to calculate communication costs.
the communication cost can be statically calculated and the size of the objects can be statically inferred in a language with session-based communication primitives.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) How can we design a session-based object-oriented programming language that is suitable for distributed systems and allows the calculation of communication costs?
the design and development of a programming language for the creation of interactive, distributed systems that can be used for the creation of mobile applications.
the design and implementation of a language with communication primitives and session types, and with a compiler that can calculate the communication cost of an application.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the session-based object-oriented programming paradigm is an excellent choice for developing high-performance, real-time, distributed applications.
the use of the session type approach in the context of the object-oriented language is a promising research area, which is worth further investigation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to calculate communication costs for objects in an OO language with session-based communication.
we have shown that session types and size information can be integrated into an object-oriented language and used to calculate the cost of sending objects.
we are working to create a language with the expressiveness of object-orientation, the communication primitives of session-based communication, and the ability to calculate communication costs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the session type discipline is a powerful mechanism for the design of object-oriented languages with explicit communication primitives.
the cost of communication is a first-class citizen and can be used to govern the interaction among different objects.
session types can provide an elegant and efficient way of statically calculating the cost of communicating objects in a distributed system.
